recordedOnly.note: distinctComponents STOPPED BEING GATED, 2026-08-31, after the capture was read key by key instead of as a bare number. It counts distinct keys in the render tally, and in a production build those keys are MINIFIED identifiers — 'lj', 'dr', 'K' — because the collector reads `type.displayName || type.name`. Where the minifier hands two components the same short name, that name expands into one key per ancestor path, so a single component can contribute a dozen keys made of other minified names. 69 of the 96 keys in the capture that prompted this are exactly that, and the capture records them in `unminifiedComponentKeys`. The number therefore measures the bundler's name assignment, not the app's component set: a rename or a module-order shift anywhere merges or splits a key and moves it. Measured, not argued: one commit that added a single component to the Live screen (a screen the Inventory-change window does not even render) produced a capture in which 71 of 96 keys had a DIFFERENT string from its parent commit while the count and the structure were unchanged; and develop's own tip measured 94/16814 on CI and 96/17534 on a developer machine from the same source. This is the same non-portability that moved the gate 95 -> 93 and then 93 -> 94 within one day, each time recorded as though it were attributable. The counts are gated as RANGES instead, which is what they could always carry: a real regression here is the grid re-rendering an order of magnitude more, not a component type appearing. A quiet window is still exactly ZERO and is gated at zero, for a structural reason rather than an empirical one: the fixture ticker's ~100 commits per 5s all carry an identical body, so no account:changed is emitted at all. The one-item change (dropping a single gear item from a 221-item inventory) costs ~16800 on CI and ~17500 locally across 8 commits, because the grid re-renders all ~220 cards and their per-card subtrees for a change to one of them — a real, pre-existing property of that grid this instrument makes visible, not something any of these measurements introduced. The ranges hold both environments with margin. If a run lands outside them, that is a genuine finding to investigate rather than a number to widen. RE-CAPTURED 2026-09-07, and the reason is the top bar's stage order rather than the grid: the bar now drops its tab words before its actions, so a window under ~1216px draws six glyph tabs, and a glyph tab is named by a design-system tooltip — five Tooltip components per tab plus a provider, all of them re-rendering with the shell on an account change. Measured as a 2x2 on one machine, same fixture, same build mode: at a 1280px window develop and the change both read 19078, and at a 1024px window develop reads 18886 while the change reads 19526 (+640, +3.4%), with distinctComponents 108 -> 156 over the same pair. The change costs nothing where the tabs keep their words and costs the tooltips where they do not, which is the trade the stage order was reordered to make. CI runs at 1024px — develop's own CI number is 18886, the same figure that window reproduces here — so the runner sits on the glyph side of it. The band's old ceiling of 19000 was ALREADY exhausted before any of this: develop's tip measures 19078 at the 1280px default window, 78 over, and passed CI only because CI's screen is narrower. So the new band holds four measured points — 18886, 19078, 19526 — with the same shape of margin the old one had, rather than being widened to the smallest number that would go green. RE-BASELINED 2026-10-06, because the offline fixture grew from 221 to 228 items, not because any component changed. Develop's own CI run before this change (the last one that ran this job) read 20399 over 8 commits, 193 distinct keys, at the runner's window: inside the 17500-21000 band with 601 to spare, the app having grown since the figures above were taken. The change's CI run read 21487 (8 commits, 193 distinct), 487 over that band. The difference, 21487 - 20399 = 1088, is exactly what the fixture's seven new items cost, measured by building the change once and running the instrument hidden (BFC_HIDE_WINDOWS=1, a 1280x800 window) on four fixtures against that one build, with identical results on every repeat: the previous 221-item fixture reads 20591; the same 221 items carrying the new per-item fields reads 20591, so the fields cost nothing; adding the three closed chests (two hero cages and a gem chest) reads 21247 (+656); adding the four Chance Stones reads 21023 (+432); all seven together read 21679 (+1088 = 656 + 432). The local window is wider than CI's and every local figure sits a constant 192 above its CI twin (20591 vs 20399, 21679 vs 21487), so the change's code adds nothing on the old fixture: the CI-to-CI difference and the local old-to-new difference are the same 1088. The mechanism is the one the paragraph above already records as a pre-existing property of the grid: one gear item leaving re-renders every card, and the seven items draw five more cards (the stones stack into one card per rarity, the chests do not), taking the grid from 146 to 151 cards. The tallies show it card for card: each of 26 per-card keys, among them the price Tooltip's Provider, Root, Trigger and Portal chain, rises by exactly 5 x 8 = 40 (1168 to 1208 for the per-card components, 448 to 488 for the tooltip chain, 56 to 61 tooltip-bearing cards: all five new cards carry the price tooltip). A stacked card also draws the stack glyph, the one key that rose by 16 (two stacked stone cards x 8 commits), and two of the three chests draw the price portal pair, the keys that rose by 16 instead of 24 in the chests-only run. The new kind having no wiki art costs nothing: with no icon source the tile omits its image, so a stone card comes to 27 renders per commit against a chest's 26 or 28. Nothing the change adds to the design system or the table is rendered on the Inventory screen. The band now holds four measured points, 20399 (develop's CI before the change), 20591 (the same code locally on the old fixture), 21487 (the change's CI) and 21679 (the change locally), with the same shape of margin the old one had: about 7% under the lowest and over the highest. The next fixture growth moves the figure by the same per-card amount, about 27 renders x 8 commits = 216 per added card.
